Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice and plant materials; Acacia pennata (Thembra) reported in some accounts
Equipment: Household vessels and starter cakes; exact equipment varies
Method_Description: Traditional starter preparation is described in published studies; botanical composition should be recorded per source/locality.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Not standardised across all households
Variation_by_Locality: Variation must be verified; do not treat a reported plant list as universal.
Evidence_Notes: Summary of published descriptions; requires source-by-source extraction.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; Bairing and Bora rice reported
Equipment: Covered earthen or bamboo vessels
Method_Description: Rice is cooled, mixed with starter and fermented; one study reports approximately five to seven days, depending on conditions.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: About 5–7 days reported in one study; not a universal standard
Variation_by_Locality: Household, seasonal and locality variations need verification.
Evidence_Notes: Do not treat a reported duration as a universal recipe or safety validation.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Fermented rice mixture
Equipment: Collection equipment not fully standardised in current record
Method_Description: Liquid is collected from fermented material; fresh and preserved forms are reported.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Preservation duration and storage conditions not yet established
Variation_by_Locality: Need detailed source extraction and local confirmation.
Evidence_Notes: Current record is preliminary.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; rice varieties vary by source and locality
Equipment: Household vessels; detailed equipment varies
Method_Description: The Majuli 2026 study describes cooked rice mixed with powdered E’pob, transferred to an earthen pot and fermented for 7–10 days; water is mixed with fermented rice, stirred until milky, then sieved. Other studies also describe Noggin Apong as a liquid extracted from fermented rice without ash addition.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 7–10 days reported in the Majuli 2026 study; not a universal standard
Variation_by_Locality: Must be checked across districts and households.
Evidence_Notes: Source-specific full-text method from SRC-084; sampled villages are unnamed. Do not universalise duration or equipment.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; ash from rice husks or bran reported
Equipment: Household fermentation vessels; full apparatus needs source-level verification
Method_Description: The Majuli 2026 study describes cooked rice mixed with ash collected from partially burned dry paddy straw and paddy husk, then mixed with powdered E’pob and fermented in an earthen pot. Other literature reports variants including rice-husk/bran ash; exact materials vary by source.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: No universal duration recorded in this archive
Variation_by_Locality: Ash material and process details require locality-specific comparison.
Evidence_Notes: SRC-084 describes Po:ro extraction by filtration, not distillation. Preserve source-specific process descriptions and investigate conflicting classifications elsewhere.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Fermented rice mixture with reported rice-husk/bran ash addition
Equipment: Distillation equipment not sufficiently documented in current sources
Method_Description: Process classification is unresolved across the literature. Some sources describe Poro/Por Apong as distilled; the full-text Majuli 2026 study describes fermented rice-ash mixture being diluted/washed with water and filtered through a conical bamboo Ta:suk basket, with no distillation stage in that account. Do not treat filtration as distillation.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Majuli study reports fermentation commonly taking 1–2 weeks depending on starter amount and temperature; other source durations vary
Variation_by_Locality: Material and extraction method may vary by locality; direct community-level process comparison needed.
Evidence_Notes: Explicit source conflict: SRC-084 describes filtration; SRC-005/SRC-006 and other records have been read as describing distillation. Verify original methods and terminology before deciding whether the products differ or one account is inaccurate.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Soaked glutinous rice and locally collected plant materials
Equipment: Pounder; drying surfaces; earthen storage container reported in one Sivasagar study
Method_Description: A 2023 field study documented ÉPOP preparation using 31 plant species across 22 families in Sivasagar district; plant materials were dried, crushed and mixed with soaked glutinous rice, formed into cakes, inoculated with prior starter material and dried for storage.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: One study reports prepared starter cakes can be stored up to six months; this is not a universal guarantee.
Variation_by_Locality: Plant lists and preparation customs vary and should be attributed to the particular village/study.
Evidence_Notes: The 31-species inventory belongs to the sampled Sivasagar study and must not be universalised to all Mising communities.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice and locally collected plant parts; ingredients differ by study and village
Starter_Culture: Mod pitha; Chuzae-pitha in a Dhemaji study
Equipment: Wooden grinder (dheki), bamboo sieving/handling implements and drying surfaces are reported in older fieldwork
Method_Description: A 2007 ethnobotanical study describes rice and dried plant materials ground together, shaped into starter cakes and inoculated/maintained using older starter material. A 2010 study records a different locality-specific Deori starter plant inventory in Dhemaji.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Starter preparation seasons September–October and February–March are reported by a later survey for its study area only.
Variation_by_Locality: Plant lists and local starter names vary across villages and studies.
Evidence_Notes: Do not combine the 32-species 2007 inventory and the 15-species Dhemaji inventory into one universal recipe.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice and prepared starter cake; water is used in the documented process
Starter_Culture: Mod pitha; Chuzae-pitha in a Dhemaji study
Equipment: Earthen fermentation vessel (koloh/disoh in one older account); vessel terminology varies by source
Method_Description: Older fieldwork describes cooked or prepared rice inoculated with starter and fermented in a covered vessel; liquid is strained before serving. Exact steps differ across publications and should be transcribed source by source.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: One 2007 study reports 3–4 days in summer and about a week in winter; this is a historical, study-specific observation, not a universal process standard.
Variation_by_Locality: Season, vessel, starter and household practice need current verification.
Evidence_Notes: Do not present old fermentation durations or storage claims as food-safety guidance.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Fermented rice mixture and liquid
Equipment: Straining basket/utensil reported in older fieldwork
Method_Description: The fermented material is strained to obtain the beverage; a 2007 account reports seasonal differences in taste and keeping time.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: One 2007 account reports up to about one month in winter and 2–3 weeks in summer before souring; not a universal shelf-life or safety guarantee.
Variation_by_Locality: Storage conditions and current practice require field verification.
Evidence_Notes: Historical sensory and storage observations must not be treated as validated shelf-life recommendations.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Water-soaked rice and plant materials; Croton joufra (Marthu) is described as a principal ingredient in the 2006 field paper; other plants/substitutes reported in surveys
Equipment: Wooden mortar (long) and pestle (lingpum); bamboo sieve (ingkrung); sun/fire-place drying described in a historical account
Method_Description: Teron (2006) describes soaked rice and Marthu leaves being pounded, previously prepared thap being added, and the mixture shaped into flat cakes and dried. Other studies report additional plants or substitutions; keep each inventory tied to its source.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: One historical account reports 2–5 days of drying depending on conditions; not a universal specification.
Variation_by_Locality: Starter ingredients and substitutes vary across sources and localities.
Evidence_Notes: Do not merge plant inventories from different studies into one universal recipe; ethnomedicinal claims are not clinical evidence.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice, water and powdered thap
Equipment: Large covered container; source-specific vessels
Method_Description: Cooked rice is cooled and mixed with powdered thap; the 2012 survey describes an initial fermentation followed by additional fermentation after water is added. Teron (2006) also describes the fermented rice beverage as Hor-alank. Preserve source-specific sequences rather than combining them into a single definitive method.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: A 2012 survey reports an initial 2 days followed by 2–4 further days depending on season in its study context; not a universal process standard.
Variation_by_Locality: Season, rice, vessel and process vary and need current verification.
Evidence_Notes: Historical descriptions only; no food-safety validation is implied.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Fermented Hor-alank
Starter_Culture: Thap is used upstream in Hor-alank fermentation
Equipment: Traditional still called Bhot in Teron (2006); improved stills also discussed
Method_Description: Hor-arak is described as the distilled form obtained from Hor-alank. The historical paper documents traditional and improved still apparatus, but the archive needs further extraction of diagrams, terminology and locality-specific differences.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: No single universal duration or equipment specification recorded.
Variation_by_Locality: Still design and use need locality-specific and current documentation.
Evidence_Notes: This record documents cultural/process history, not instructions for producing or consuming alcohol.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice or rice paste and locally used plant parts; species and parts differ between published inventories
Equipment: Wooden mortar and pestle; paddy straw or other drying surface reported
Method_Description: Deka and Sarma (2010) describe soaked rice and selected plant parts being ground into a paste, shaped into flat cakes and dried. Bhuyan and Baishya (2013) summarise a similar starter-cake tradition and list plant materials for Jonga mod. The 2023 Chokot study describes Bakhor/Phap as a plant-based starter. These source-specific inventories must remain separate.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: The 2010 paper describes a drying stage; exact conditions vary by source and should not be treated as a standard.
Variation_by_Locality: Starter names and plant ingredients differ by locality and source; botanical identification needs verification.
Evidence_Notes: Ethnobotanical lists record reported traditional use, not evidence of clinical efficacy or a universal formula.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice and prepared starter cake; water is reported in descriptions of the finished beverage
Equipment: Earthen fermentation vessel; banana-leaf cover and a bamboo-net insert are described in a 2013 review summary of the 2010 study
Method_Description: Published descriptions state that cooled cooked rice is mixed with powdered starter and fermented in a covered vessel; some accounts describe adding water and straining the fermented mass. Exact sequence and duration differ across sources and must not be collapsed into one definitive recipe.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: A 2010/2013 account reports seasonal differences in fermentation duration; treat as historical study-specific observation, not a universal process standard or safety guidance.
Variation_by_Locality: Village, season, starter, vessel and fermentation sequence need current verification.
Evidence_Notes: Archive record summarises published ethnographic process descriptions and is not production or food-safety guidance.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Starter culture sampled from Rabha household preparation
Equipment: Laboratory analysis of starter culture; traditional household preparation is documented separately
Method_Description: Bhattacharjee et al. (2023) analysed microbial populations in Chokot starter culture collected in Rasikbill Rabha basti, Cooch Behar. The study reports bacterial genera including Bacillus, Arthrobacter, Lactobacillus, Ilyobacter, Clostridium and Lactococcus. These are results from the sampled starter, not a universal microbiome for all Rabha beverages.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Samples collected in February 2022.
Variation_by_Locality: Microbial profiles may vary by household, locality, season and starter preparation.
Evidence_Notes: Do not infer health benefits or safety from microbial presence alone; laboratory findings are sample-specific.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice powder or rice paste, water and selected plant parts; species lists differ by study
Starter_Culture: Vekur pitha / Xaj-pitha / Xajor pitha; Haaj-pitha is another reported starter term
Equipment: Wooden mortar and pestle; banana leaves or other drying surfaces; covered vessel
Method_Description: Das, Deka and Miyaji (2012) describe washing/drying selected plant parts, grinding them with rice and water, shaping oval cakes and drying them before use. Their Sivasagar inventory includes Oldenlandia corymbosa, Lygodium sp., Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides, Centella asiatica, Cissampelos pareira and Piper nigrum. Treat this as one source-specific inventory.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: About five days of drying reported in the 2012 survey; other accounts differ.
Variation_by_Locality: Plant species, plant parts, starter names and proportions vary across sources and households.
Evidence_Notes: Published ethnobotanical documentation is source-specific; plant use is not proof of medical efficacy or a universal formula.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Glutinous or non-glutinous rice; cooked/partly cooked rice and powdered starter; water added later in one description
Equipment: Earthen pot (koloh/kalah); banana leaves; cloth for straining in one survey; raised bench over fireplace described in one study
Method_Description: The 2012 survey describes partly cooked rice cooled on banana leaves, mixed with powdered starter and fermented in a sealed earthen pot for 3–5 days, after which water is added and the mass strained. Bora et al. (2016) describe a liquid called rohi collected during the fermentation setup and diluted to serve as xaj. Preserve this source-level difference rather than combining it into one definitive recipe.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: A 3–5 day fermentation period is reported in the 2012 survey; not a universal standard.
Variation_by_Locality: Sequence, vessel, cover material, duration and relationship between rohi and xaj need locality-specific verification.
Evidence_Notes: Historical description only; not a food-safety or production instruction. Fermentation duration is not a safety guarantee.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Xaj-pitha starter cakes sampled from rural Ahom households
Equipment: Sterile sample containers and laboratory microbiology/metagenomic methods
Method_Description: Bora et al. (2016) analysed Xaj-pitha collected from five rural households in Titabar subdivision, Jorhat district. Keot et al. (2020) sampled 60 starter cultures across 12 clusters in six Upper Brahmaputra Valley districts and investigated microbial quality and possible contaminants. These are findings about the sampled starters, not all household batches.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 2016 sample collection: 20 August 2014; 2020 study used a multi-district sample design.
Variation_by_Locality: Microbial profiles may vary by household, district, season and preparation method; the 2016 metagenomic sample was from Titabar.
Evidence_Notes: Laboratory findings are sample-specific; neither presence of a microorganism nor traditional use establishes safety or health benefit.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice powder; plant parts; portion of existing starter
Equipment: Mortar/pulverising device; cloth, rice straw or fern leaves; bamboo/other storage containers
Method_Description: Narzary et al. describe rice powder mixed with herbs and mother starter, covered for microbial growth and then sun-dried. Plant combinations varied across six starter samples.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 3–4 days covered; 2–3 days sun-drying reported in 2021 study
Variation_by_Locality: Plant lists vary by locality and availability.
Evidence_Notes: Starter method and microbial findings are sample-specific, not a universal recipe.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; plant-and-rice starter cake
Equipment: Bamboo mat, banana leaves and covered vessel in source-specific accounts
Method_Description: The 2014 paper describes Jou from fermented cooked rice with Amao. A 2025 paper calls the direct fermented product Joubidwi and distinguishes it from stored Joufinai. Keep terminology differences visible.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Several days in source-specific accounts; no universal duration established
Variation_by_Locality: Rice variety, vessel, starter and naming vary by locality.
Evidence_Notes: Jumai may refer to the rice/starter mixture in one source, not the finished drink.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; powdered Amao
Starter_Culture: Amao reported in related Bodo starter literature
Equipment: Bamboo mat (songrai), banana leaves, earthen pot (maldang) or bucket, bamboo sieve (janta)
Method_Description: A Bodo heritage page describes cooked rice cooled on a mat, mixed with Amao, covered with banana leaves and fermented in a vessel with a bamboo sieve. Not a universal GI specification.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Page reports 1–2 days before transfer and another 5–6 days before collection.
Variation_by_Locality: Needs locality-specific corroboration and comparison with official statement of case.
Evidence_Notes: GI status is official; process details here come from a heritage page.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice and Amao starter
Equipment: Bamboo mat (dhara), banana leaves and vessel called hadi in 2025 account
Method_Description: A 2025 study describes cooked rice cooled, mixed with Amao, placed on banana leaves overnight, then stored in a vessel; colour and liquid yield varied with storage duration.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 3, 6, 10 and 12 months reported; article also mentions 1–2 years broadly.
Variation_by_Locality: Vessel, temperature, duration and name require household-level verification.
Evidence_Notes: Source-specific account, not a recommended preparation or safety protocol.

Stage: Distillation of fermented rice-based mixture (historical account)
Ingredients_or_Materials: Fermented rice mixture called jumai in 2014 paper
Equipment: Traditional distillation apparatus; detailed equipment source-specific
Method_Description: Basumatary et al. describe gwran as distilled alcohol from fermented rice mixture. Relationship to GI-defined product should be checked against its official statement of case.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Duration not consistently established.
Variation_by_Locality: Substrate and equipment vary or are incompletely specified.
Evidence_Notes: Keep separate from fruit-based Jougwran descriptions.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Jackfruit (Kanthal) or banana (Kola); Amao starter
Equipment: Local still; 2025 paper describes perforated earthen bowl, receiver and cooling vessel
Method_Description: Deka et al. document Kanthal-Jougwran from jackfruit and Kola-Jougwran from banana followed by distillation. Do not assume identical to rice-based gwran or GI-defined product.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Up to 3 days for Kanthal; 3–4 days for Kola in the reported study.
Variation_by_Locality: Fruit substrate and names differ by variant.
Evidence_Notes: Field-study description from Kokrajhar-area interviews, not a universal recipe.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice; plant materials reported for starter-cake preparation; cooked rice including Bora, Chakuwa and ordinary rice
Equipment: Exact household equipment not established in accessible abstract
Method_Description: Gogoi (2021) documents a traditional plant-and-rice starter cake used with cooked rice to prepare Saj/Laopani among Chaodang knowledge holders. The study reports 81 plant species across its sample; this is not a universal ingredient list or fixed recipe.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Fermentation duration not established from accessible abstract.
Variation_by_Locality: Starter plants and procedures may vary by village, household, season and plant availability.
Evidence_Notes: Peer-reviewed field study; retrieve full text for precise sequence and equipment. Avoid inferring current practice from historical documentation.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice and locally gathered plant materials; exact list varies by study
Equipment: Household equipment needs full-text extraction
Method_Description: Published Tiwa studies describe a rice-and-plant starter cake called Bakhor, used with rice to prepare Zu/Chu. Do not combine plant lists from separate studies into one standard recipe.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Exact duration and temperature not established consistently across sources.
Variation_by_Locality: Ingredients and procedures may vary by locality, household, season and plant availability.
Evidence_Notes: Based on the 2020 Tiwa field study and 2023 ethnobotanical survey; detailed sequence and equipment require source-level verification.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice; Glycyrrhiza glabra bark is reported for the Dabai starter in one 2026 southern Assam account
Starter_Culture: Dabai (2026 account); Dawai (2024 article; naming relationship unresolved)
Equipment: Clay/earthen pot; sun-drying surface; straining implement
Method_Description: One 2026 account says rice is soaked overnight and ground with Yastimadhu/licorice bark to make flat rounded starter cakes, which are sun-dried. Cooked rice is cooled, mixed with starter, covered in a clay pot, fermented, and strained. A separate 2024 paper reports Tea-tribe Haria with a starter called dawai but does not establish that it is identical in composition to Dabai.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 2026 account: about 3–4 days; 2024 paper describes a broad 4–5 days to one week for the studied beverages and states conditions vary seasonally
Variation_by_Locality: No village-specific recipe comparison yet; starter spelling/composition needs corroboration
Evidence_Notes: These are source-specific descriptions, not a universal recipe. The 2024 paper analysed 3 Haria samples as part of 15 beverage samples across five communities; microbiome results should not be treated as proof of health benefit or safety.

Stage: Starter preparation and fermentation (generic Zao account)
Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice; bark of the locally named Nduihi gei plant; plant identity not confirmed
Equipment: Bamboo tray; clay pot; banana leaves; subtype-specific filter/basket and gourd vessel
Method_Description: One southern Assam account describes cooking rice and spreading it on a bamboo tray. Starter Nduihi is made by mixing soaked rice with ground bark of the Nduihi gei plant, forming a flattened cake and sun-drying it. The dried starter and cooled cooked rice are placed in a clay pot covered with banana leaves and left to ferment. A separate 2020 ethnographic source describes multiple Zeme beverages and different processing methods; those should be recorded separately after subtype reconciliation.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: A 2024 review table gives 3–5 days for Zeme Zou based on Atungbou (2020); exact duration and conditions vary by named preparation
Variation_by_Locality: Names, substrates and processing differ among Tekuizou/Zousang, Tamzou/Lingtakzou and Nduizou in the 2020 account; do not treat as a universal recipe
Evidence_Notes: Plant identity of Nduihi gei is unresolved in the 2026 study. A named Nduizou account describes liquid dripping through a basket and optional further distillation; this method is not assumed for all Zao/Zou.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice; bark of Acacia pennata, called Zangzu in the 2026 study
Equipment: Starter-cake grinding/mixing tools; earthen or aluminum vessel; banana leaves or sacks used as covers in the cross-community process description
Method_Description: The 2026 southern Assam account describes Hmar Chol starter made from rice grains and bark of Zangzu (Acacia pennata), shaped into round or flat cakes and dried. Cooked rice is cooled, mixed with starter, fermented in a covered vessel and filtered. The 2024 microbiome study sampled Hmar Zu before distillation. Cross-community vessel descriptions should not be mistaken for a complete, uniform Hmar household recipe.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: About 3–5 days depending on season in the 2024 study's summary table; general cross-community range is several days up to one week
Variation_by_Locality: Exact Hmar sample villages and local variations not identified in the reviewed article passages
Evidence_Notes: The starter plant is identified as Acacia pennata/Zangzu by the 2026 study. The sample-based microbiome study does not establish safety, health benefit, or the full range of Hmar beverage products.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Glutinous/local rice; multiple plant parts incorporated into Mod pitha (full species list should be preserved source-by-source)
Starter_Culture: Mod pitha / Saul pitha / Saoul pitha
Equipment: Dheki wooden grinder; Saloni bamboo sieve; heat-sterilized earthen pot; Sakoni filter net, as described in 2023 study
Method_Description: The 2023 study describes collecting and washing plant parts, drying them on a Saloni, soaking rice overnight, grinding the rice and plant materials in a Dheki, and adding a small amount of old Mod pitha to the powder. Starter cakes are shaped and dried. Cooked/glutinous rice is cooled, mixed with starter, placed in a heat-sterilized earthen pot and fermented; the mass is then filtered to obtain Rohi. Exact household variations should be retained.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 2023 account: 4–5 days generally; approximately one week in winter
Variation_by_Locality: Study centered on Jokai area, Dibrugarh; the paper notes seasonal differences and local variants in naming
Evidence_Notes: A 2026 article studies Rohi and Sepa together but does not provide Sepa-specific detail in its accessible abstract. Do not assume their processes are identical solely because both use Mod pitha.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice; plant materials in Mod pitha starter, according to the 2026 article abstract
Equipment: Not established in the accessible abstract
Method_Description: The 2026 paper identifies Sepa as a fermented rice beer prepared using Mod pitha. Detailed process stages, ingredient proportions, equipment and differences from Rohi are not stated in the accessible abstract and are deliberately left open pending full-text review.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Not established for Sepa in the accessible abstract
Variation_by_Locality: Not established
Evidence_Notes: Do not copy the Rohi recipe into Sepa's record until the full article or another source explicitly supports the same method.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Black rice; exact proportions and batch-specific ingredients not fully established in reviewed text
Starter_Culture: Aaroi is reported for Rohi Modh in the article; Black Rohi Modh starter-specific details require confirmation
Equipment: Not established for the Black Rohi Modh sample in reviewed text
Method_Description: A 2026 peer-reviewed study separately analyzed a household Black Rohi Modh batch and a Rohi Modh batch. It identifies glutinous rice and aaroi starter for Rohi Modh and describes a four-day fermentation for Rohi Modh; those details are not automatically assigned to Black Rohi Modh. Preserve the black-rice sample as a provisional variant until full sample-specific method and local terminology are confirmed.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Four days reported for Rohi Modh; Black Rohi Modh-specific duration not established
Variation_by_Locality: One household batch per beverage; no independent biological replication across production events
Evidence_Notes: Study provides microbiome and metabolomics measurements, but technical triplicates do not represent independent household batches. Do not infer clinical benefits from antioxidant assays or pathway annotations.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; powdered Wansi starter; exact quantities and rice variety not specified
Equipment: Sealed vessel; bamboo sieve/dekeli
Method_Description: The 2024 review describes cooked rice mixed with powdered Wansi, placed in a sealed vessel with a bamboo sieve to collect liquid, then kept in a dark warm place for fermentation. Do not treat this as a universal Garo recipe.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 5–7 days reported in the secondary review
Variation_by_Locality: Exact Assam locality and variation by village or household not established; do not transfer the Chubitchi Meghalaya method to Chu without evidence.
Evidence_Notes: Review-level description only; confirm against primary ethnography or Garo-language/community sources before treating details as canonical.

Stage: Laboratory characterization of named sample varieties; traditional preparation incompletely documented
Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice; exact substrate and recipe details need full-text review
Equipment: Not specified in accessible abstract
Method_Description: The 2025 study identifies Opo as the traditional starter and analyzes Nyishi rice-wine samples labelled Tisar, Kecha and Adak. The accessible abstract does not establish the exact household preparation sequence or assign each sample to a named village.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Not established
Variation_by_Locality: Variety labels and preparation may differ by locality; exact sampling locality unresolved.
Evidence_Notes: Laboratory measurements characterize collected samples, not community-wide recipe or health effects.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Sticky/glutinous rice, black or white varieties; starter cake material not fully specified
Equipment: Cooking pot; Go dal flat bamboo basket; covered pot; bottle/container
Method_Description: Cook sticky rice without making it mushy, spread it over a traditional flat bamboo basket (Go dal) and cool; mix Chol evenly; transfer to a pot, place charcoal over the rice as described by the source, cover the pot and keep it in sunlight or a warm kitchen location. After fermentation, separate the semi-liquid top fraction called aning from the solid Anthom mass.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 3–7 days reported by the 2019 article
Variation_by_Locality: Source-specific account; village and household variation not mapped.
Evidence_Notes: Do not treat the described process as universal. Aning is a liquid fraction in this account, not proven to be a separate canonical beverage.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; small amount of water
Starter_Culture: Ipoh / Si-ye / Paa (terms reported for different groups)
Equipment: Wide-bottom cooking vessel; covered fermentation vessel
Method_Description: The source describes mixing starter cake with cooked rice, transferring the mixture to a covered vessel with a little water, fermenting, then diluting with drinking water before serving.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 3–5 days incubation reported in the 2007 account
Variation_by_Locality: The article reports terms and a method broadly across communities; exact community-specific recipe allocation is not established.
Evidence_Notes: Historical ethnological description; not a universal or current household recipe.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; paddy husk blackened over heat; Ipoh starter cake; hot water for extraction
Equipment: Conical bamboo basket (noga-baye); leaf-lined woven bamboo container (Perop); bamboo tube (Petok); wood and stone for sealing
Method_Description: The source describes mixing cooked rice with blackened paddy husk and starter, holding it in a leaf-lined conical basket, transferring it to a larger leaf-lined woven bamboo container for fermentation, then pouring hot water through portions in a bamboo tube to collect the brew. First draw is called Tok-Til in the article.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: About 3 days initial stage; about 10 days overall before filtration/extraction in this account
Variation_by_Locality: No product-specific village mapping; equipment and terms should be verified with current community sources.
Evidence_Notes: Historical ethnological description; do not generalize the article's broad tribal attribution.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice, preferably glutinous; locally collected plant leaves; powdered old starter culture
Starter_Culture: E’pob / Apop / Apop pitha (source spellings vary)
Equipment: Wooden pestle and mortar (Ki:per and E’gi); bamboo sieve/platform; paddy straw; earthen pot
Method_Description: The Majuli 2026 study describes cleaning and soaking rice for 2–3 hours, pounding it into powder, drying and pounding collected plant leaves, mixing plant powder and rice with some old starter culture, shaping small cakes, spreading them on a bamboo sieve with straw and Rukji leaves, sun-drying, then storing in an earthen pot plugged with Rukji leaves.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Soak 2–3 hours; sun-dry 2–3 days; starter cakes reported storable 1–2 months
Variation_by_Locality: Plant ingredients, rice type and handling are locality-specific; do not treat the 48-species inventory as a single universal recipe.
Evidence_Notes: Full-text Majuli study (SRC-084); 48 species documented for starter-cake preparation, but the study does not name the three sampled villages in accessible text. Botanical/medicinal claims are not clinical efficacy evidence.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice and powdered E’pob; water added after fermentation
Equipment: Cooking pot, bamboo mat or banana leaves for cooling, earthen fermentation pot, sieve
Method_Description: The Majuli 2026 study describes cleaning and cooking rice, cooling it on a bamboo mat or banana leaves, mixing in powdered starter, transferring the mixture to an earthen pot, fermenting, then mixing some fermented rice with water and stirring until milky before sieving the liquid.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: 7–10 days for fermentation in the Majuli study; source-specific, not a safety validation or universal standard
Variation_by_Locality: Rice varieties, plant additives, vessels and fermentation duration may vary; the three study villages are not named in the accessible text.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; ash from partially burned dry paddy straw and paddy husk; powdered E’pob; water
Equipment: Earthen fermentation pot; conical bamboo Ta:suk strainer lined with leaves and straw; collection vessel
Method_Description: The Majuli 2026 study describes partially burning paddy straw and husk and retaining the ash; cooked rice is mixed with ash and powdered starter and fermented in an earthen pot. The fermented mixture is transferred to a conical bamboo Ta:suk basket lined with leaves and a straw bundle, and water is poured over it in stages; the filtrate is collected as Apong. This account documents extraction by filtration, not distillation.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Approximately 1–2 weeks fermentation reported, depending on starter quantity and warmer/cooler conditions; source-specific
Variation_by_Locality: Do not assume all Mising communities use identical ash, vessels, leaf liners, fermentation times or extraction methods.
Evidence_Notes: Full-text Majuli method from SRC-084. It conflicts with other descriptions that label Poro Apong as distilled; the discrepancy is explicitly unresolved and requires source/terminology review.
